questions.q: Why is 'rollback' often not realistic for a major-version in-place upgrade?
options: In-place upgrades are always reversible with a single command
Compatibility level automatically reverses on failure
Rollback only applies to Cumulative Updates, never to major version upgrades
SQL Server does not support attaching or restoring a database backed up on a newer major version onto an older-version instance
questions.explain: The on-disk format and internal metadata move forward, not backward, so a downgrade path generally doesn't exist once the upgrade has touched the databases.

questions.q: What does 'rollback' actually mean for a major in-place upgrade, per this lesson?
options: Simply lowering the compatibility level back to its old value
Restoring a pre-upgrade backup onto a separately available instance still running the old version
Uninstalling the latest Cumulative Update
Reversing the upgrade in place using SQL Server Setup
questions.explain: Since in-place downgrade isn't supported, real rollback requires restoring a backup elsewhere, onto an old-version instance kept available for that purpose.

questions.q: What makes a pre-change backup actually useful as a rollback safety net, according to this lesson?
options: It was taken more than a month before the change
It has been test-restored to verify it works, not just confirmed to have completed successfully
It was taken after the upgrade instead of before
It is stored on the same drive as the live database
questions.explain: A backup that 'ran successfully' but was never test-restored is an unverified assumption, not a real safety net.

questions.q: Why does this lesson describe side-by-side migration as 'a rollback strategy in disguise'?
options: It automatically restores the old version if the new one fails a health check
The old instance is left running and untouched, so rollback is just re-pointing applications back to it — fast and genuinely reversible
Side-by-side migration eliminates the need for any backups
It is only used for Cumulative Updates, not major upgrades
questions.explain: Because the old instance keeps running untouched during a side-by-side migration, reverting is simply re-pointing connections, unlike an in-place upgrade's backup-and-restore dependency.

questions.q: What should be decided BEFORE an upgrade, not improvised during it, per this lesson?
options: Whether backups are enabled at all
The exact wording of the maintenance window email
The decision point — who has authority to call a rollback, and what specific symptoms trigger that call
Which edition of SQL Server to install
questions.explain: Deciding the rollback trigger and decision-maker under pressure, in the moment, is how bad calls get made — it needs to be agreed on in advance.
